newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bond pullbacks seen short-lived.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bond pullbacks seen short-lived.

text.p: Pullbacks in U.S. Treasury bond futures are likely to be short-lived in the near term, despite a variety of overbought signals after recent rallies, technical analysts said.

"Even though the bond market is overbought here, the trend is still intact and it's well supported," said Terence Gabriel, a technical analyst at I.D.E.A. "So I'm still looking for a move up to that 115-17/32 (December 3 high in September T-bond futures)."
September T-bonds were off 4/32 at 114-00 in late morning trade after hitting a seven-month high of 114-15/32 on Friday.

Analysts said short-term oscillators, such as the daily stochastic, were clearly in overbought territory. But they noted that it was not unusual for the indicators to be at high levels during a strong bull run.

Gabriel said interest rate-sensitive instruments -- like bonds, bank stocks and the Dow Jones Utility index -- have continued outperforming commodity price indicators -- such as gold, gold stocks or the Commodity Research Bureau index.
"Such pronounced relative outperformance on the part of the interest-sensitives...is quite a positive sign," he noted.

On the weekly continuous chart, T-bond futures last week broke above a trendline drawn from the January 1996 high and the December 1996 high. That former resistance line comes in this week at about 113-10/32 to 113-13/32.
"Last week there was a decisive closing penetration of that line," Gabriel said. "I would expect if we dip back down, that broken trendline will now act as support."
He added that the February high of 113-9/32 also lurked in the area, offering further support.
Alex Saitta, a technical analyst at Salomon Brothers, said he was also skeptical of the overbought oscillator readings.
However, he noted that volume in call options has exceeded that in puts at an alarming rate in recent sessions, prompting him to turn neutral from bullish for now.
"My feeling is the T-bond will come off this week," he said. "If the break is on high volume, I'll turn bearish. If the decline is on low volume, I'll turn bullish at support."

Saitta said his study of T-bond prices in the past seven years showed that when the call/put ratio in a 20-day period exceeded 1.25, the market was more likely to move favorably for the bears in the following 10-day period. Likewise, he said a ratio below 0.80 has been a valid bullish signal.
